findings.issue: Task 14 is missing the mandatory `## Reviewers` section entirely. The H2 headings between Details and Post-completion (## Summary verdict, ## Scope, ## Findings by focus area, etc.) appear inside a fenced code block that documents the *audit report* template — they are not real document sections. The file goes directly from `## Details` (ending at the Implementation hints bullets) to `## Post-completion`. The template (and task-creator agent rules §10) mandates a Reviewers section even when reviewers=[] — it should contain a sentinel like 'None. This task is self-verifying — its output is the audit report; no downstream reviewer.' (Task 15 does this correctly at line 170-172.)
findings.fix: Insert a `## Reviewers` section between the Details and Post-completion sections containing one short paragraph noting that this is a self-verifying audit task with no downstream reviewers (mirroring Task 15's pattern). Example body: 'None. This task is the code-quality audit for the feature — its output (`work/migrate-to-virtual-threads/audit/code-audit.md`) is consumed by Task 17 pre-deploy QA, not by a downstream reviewer agent.'

findings.issue: Task 13 declares `depends_on: [11]` with `wave: 3`, but Task 11 also has `wave: 3`. The validator's dependency-correctness rule requires that any task with `depends_on: [X]` must have a `wave` strictly greater than X's wave. The tech-spec (line 441) intentionally bundles Task 11 → Task 12 (parallel) → Task 13 (sequential after 11) into Wave 3 to express the single-writer constraint on patterns.md, but this collapses two ordering levels into one wave label and breaks the wave-based scheduler invariant: a feature-execution agent that dispatches a wave in parallel could try to start Task 13 before Task 11 finishes, since they share wave=3.
findings.fix: Either (a) bump Task 13 to `wave: 4` and Task 14/15/16/17 to `wave: 5` to preserve strict dependency-implies-higher-wave, or (b) keep Task 13 at wave 3 but document the in-wave ordering convention explicitly in tech-spec and document that the feature-execution skill must honor `depends_on` even within a wave. Option (a) is the safer fix and aligns with the validator rule. Verify no other task has the same in-wave dependency pattern after the bump.
